description: Conversion of dwelling into five self contained flats (1 X 3 bed, 1 X 2 bed, and 3 X 1 bed); two storey rear extension; alterations and extensions to roof; landscaping; separate amenity space; parking; bin/cycle stores; external alterations
decision_conditions: <p>By reasons of the lack of private outdoor amenity spaces for the proposed Flats B, C, D and E, the adverse vertical stacking issues between the proposed flats and the proposed first floor side window serving a habitable room in Flat D which would overlook the neighbouring property at 105 Gordon Avenue, would result in substandard level of living accommodation for the future occupiers of the proposed dwellings, and an adverse loss of privacy to the detrimental of the amenity of the neighbouring occupiers. The proposal would therefore be contrary to policies Policies D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policies DM1, DM26 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), Technical housing standards – nationally described space standard (2015), Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance (2023) and Harrow Residential Design Guide (2010).</p>

<p>It has not been demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority that the proposed vehicle access to the site via Kenton Lane would ensure the safety of the users of the public highway, contrary to policies T4, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021) and DM42 of the Harrow Development Management Policies (2013).</p>

<p>The application fails to demonstrate how the proposed development would achieve the statutory minimum 10% Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG), as required by the Environment Act 2021. In the absence of a legal agreement to ensure the landowner would create or enhance habitats for a 30-year period, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the development would not result in a net loss of biodiversity or that it would deliver the required net gain. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies G6 of the London Plan (2021), CS1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and DM20 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).</p>
